To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TAZ is upregulated in the pancreatic cancer (PC), pancreatic juice and serum samples of patients, and is a target of miR-185.
miR-185 suppresses PC cell proliferation by directly targeting TAZ, and TAZ may serve as a novel therapeutic target for PC.
the miR-185- TAZ-ANKRD1/CRP axis is a novel mechanism of proliferation regulation in pancreatic cancer, and that TAZ is a promising diagnostic marker in pancreatic cancer.

the expression levels of TAZ in PC tissues and its upstream miRNA, miR- 185, and the regulation mechanisms of the TAZ signaling pathway.
the role of TAZ in PC and the regulation mechanisms of miR-185 in PC.
the mechanism of the proliferation of pancreatic cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miR-185 inhibits pancreatic cancer progression by targeting TAZ.
miR-185 regulates the proliferation of PC through TAZ.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miR-185 is a tumor-suppressor miRNA in pancreatic cancer.
miR-185 is a tumor suppressor in PC and TAZ is a novel oncogene in PC, and miR185 may regulate the growth of PC by targeting the TAZ signaling pathway.
the miR-185- TAZ axis is involved in the proliferation of pancreatic cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miR-185 is a tumor suppressor in pancreatic cancer and it regulates the proliferation of pancreatic cancer by targeting TAZ.
miR-185 can regulate TAZ expression, thereby affecting the proliferation of pancreatic cancer cells.
miR-185 is downregulated and TAZ is upregulated in pancreatic cancer tissues and that TAZ is a direct target of miR-185.
